thread:
Maya R: handing off primary for tonight, jumping off at 18:00 UTC. Primary = @Ajay P, secondary = @Lucy T. brief: we saw a KV-cache p99 spike earlier that affected payload timing for some routed customers (~1.3% error surface), oncall-runbook links below. i'm leaving a short checklist and the exact commands to use if the p99 creeps back up. pls ack and take over monitoring. :wave:

IncidentBot: Pager triggered 6325009901 - KV_CACHE_HIGH_P99 - severity: P2 - affected: routing/generation. first alert at 2025-11-02T16:18:21Z. auto-escalated to oncall. docs: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/pager-triage

Ajay P: acked, i'm on it. timeline so far: spike started ~16:15 UTC, transient drop after cache eviction at 16:24, then resumed briefly at 16:46. i patched a throttle config in staging; will avoid prod change unless we need immediate mitigation. main mitigations to try (in order): 1) enable prefix-kv fallback 2) restart kv-cache pods 3) scale kv-cache up by +1 replica 4) fall back traffic to lower-memory model variant. runbooks: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-fallback and https://redwood.internal/runbooks/rollout-fallbacks

Sam K: quick notes on how to check state:
```
# show pods with restart count and age
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=kv-cache -o wide
# check eviction and hit-rate metrics on grafana: dashboard KV Cache -> p50/p95/p99
```
if p99 > 250ms for more than 3 minutes, do the restart path. when restarting, drain one pod at a time and watch the autoscaler.

Lucy T: adding ops tip — if you need a fast temporary relief, enable reduced-consistency mode for the routing tier. it's in the console but here's the CLI toggle: `redctl routing set-consistency --level reduced --env prod`. this reduces strict KV reads but lowers p99. only use for <30m and inform customer-ops. also will add a mute rule for the noisy alert if it's flapping: `incidentctl mute --alert KV_CACHE_HIGH_P99 --duration 20m`.

Ajay P: if we do a restart, follow this order (copying to thread):
```
# drain and restart one pod
kubectl -n inference cordon pod/kv-cache-2
kubectl -n inference drain pod/kv-cache-2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
kubectl -n inference delete pod/kv-cache-2
# wait for new pod ready, verify metrics
```
After restart, check `cache_hit_rate` and `latency_p99`. If hit rate drops >10% consider increasing replicas.

IncidentBot: Note: muted alerts will auto-unmute after 20m. If you escalate to P1, IncidentBot will re-open channel and bump paging policies.

Maya R: customer impact notes for handoff: a subset of customers routing through eu-west-1 saw elevated latencies and a few 500s from the inference gateway between 16:15-16:50 UTC. SLO impact estimated <0.2% for the day but keep an eye on replays. if customers ask, use the staging incident template: https://redwood.internal/templates/customer-comms/staging-brief (fill timeline and mitigation).

Sam K: logs snippet from 16:20 window:```text
ERROR [kv-cache] failed to fetch prefix keys: timeout after 2000ms
WARN [gateway] retrying request id=abc123 attempt=2
```
This points to an upstream storage latency; if restarts don't help, we should throttle requests hitting the cache and route heavy customers to the low-memory model for 1 hour.

Lucy T: i'm good to be secondary and cover the 19:00->02:00 UTC window. Ajay, i can take over primary at 22:00 UTC if you want to swap earlier. i'll keep an eye on customer-ops channel and will run the mute if alerts flap. :thumbsup:

Ajay P: thanks. i'll monitor until 22:00 and escalate to you if i see repeated p99s >350ms for >5 minutes. leaving these watch checks in the thread for whoever's next:
- grafana: KV Cache -> p99 panel link: https://grafana.redwood/kv-cache/p99
- runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-fallback
- customer template: https://redwood.internal/templates/customer-comms/staging-brief

Maya R: handoff done for me — notes in the shift doc: https://redwood.internal/shifts/2025-11-02/mayaR. please post a short closeout here when the window is clear or if you hand the shift. thanks all. :rocket:
